name: Structural Blocks
description: Building materials where durability is a bot break-chance tier—not a hit-point bar. Metal Block 3 is the practical raid shell; scrap wood is for prototypes.
imageAlt: structural blocks image from Scrap Mechanic

tables.caption: Haybot block destruction chance by durability level
tables.note: Durability describes break probability per hit, not a separate hit-point bar.

tables.caption: Farmbot melee break chance by durability level
tables.note: Farmbots can destroy low-durability blocks simply by walking over them. Metal Block 3 is the practical defense ceiling.

sections.heading: Durability Is Chance, Not HP
paragraphs: When a bot hits a block, the game rolls against that block’s durability level. Soft materials fail often; high tiers almost never. That is why a thin scrap-wood “armor” wall fails on raid night even if it “looked thick.”

sections.heading: Put Expensive Material Only on Contact Faces
paragraphs: A vehicle or farm killbox should use Metal-tier blocks on the first impact surface and cheaper structure behind it. Armoring every decorative panel with Metal 3 wastes weight and Component Kit crafting time.
bullets: Wheels → bearings → frame load path first.
Raid approach wall second.
Paint and bodywork last.

sections.heading: Farmbots Punish Soft Floors
paragraphs: Farmbot melee tables show 100% break chance on durability 1–3 and still threaten mid tiers. Do not let a Farmbot path across scrap-wood decking that holds your Craftbot or ammo chests.

sections.heading: Prototype Cheap, Reinforce Proven Paths
paragraphs: Validate steering and tool mounts in scrap wood, then replace only the load paths that survived testing. That keeps early Survival mobile without committing Metal 3 to a bad chassis.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Blocks — Durability vs Haybot/Farmbot
seo.description: How Scrap Mechanic block durability works as break chance, with Haybot/Farmbot tables and when to use Metal Block 3 versus scrap wood. Verify it in-game.

name: Scrap Wood Block
description: An accessible early building block for prototypes, temporary structures, and the first vehicle frame.
imageAlt: scrap wood block image from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Build Cheap, Test Early
paragraphs: Scrap Wood is ideal when the shape is still changing. Use it to validate wheel spacing, steering clearance, and storage position, then reinforce only the parts that have proved useful.
bullets: Keep moving joints visible during the first test.
Replace exposed load paths before entering heavy combat.
Recover unused blocks instead of abandoning old prototypes.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Scrap Wood Block - Uses and Guide
seo.description: In Scrap Mechanic, use Scrap Wood Blocks for low-cost prototypes, starter vehicles, and temporary Survival structures. Verify the current role in-game.

name: Scrap Metal Block
description: An early metal building block suited to stronger frames and protected machine sections.
imageAlt: scrap metal block image from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Reinforce the Load Path
paragraphs: A full metal shell is not automatically a good vehicle. Put stronger material between wheels, suspension mounts, storage, and tools, while leaving non-critical panels light.
bullets: Protect bearings without blocking their motion.
Keep the roof lighter than the chassis.
Test steering again after every major weight increase.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Scrap Metal Block - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Use Scrap Metal Blocks for reinforced frames, protected mounts, and balanced vehicle construction in Scrap Mechanic. Confirm its current role.

name: Wood Blocks
description: General-purpose building materials available in multiple qualities for frames, walls, floors, and visual structure.
imageAlt: wood blocks image from Scrap Mechanic

facts.label: Design strength
facts.value: Easy visual separation from metal systems

sections.heading: Use Material Families Deliberately
paragraphs: Wood is useful when a build needs readable floors, walls, and non-mechanical sections. Higher-quality material should protect the areas that actually receive force rather than every decorative surface.
bullets: Separate living or storage areas from mechanical bays with color and material.
Keep engine and bearing mounts easy to inspect.
Upgrade the vulnerable edge first, not the entire build at once.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Wood Blocks - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Plan Wood Block use across frames, floors, walls, and readable base layouts in Scrap Mechanic. Check its connected uses before the next Survival run.

name: Metal Blocks
description: A family of stronger building blocks for durable frames, machine protection, and high-load structures.
imageAlt: metal blocks image from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Durability Needs a Chassis Plan
paragraphs: Metal makes sense around collision points, tool mounts, and high-value controls. On a vehicle, uncontrolled metal weight raises fuel demand and makes recovery harder.
bullets: Keep mass low and between the axles.
Do not encase serviceable parts behind permanent layers.
Use lighter material for wide decorative panels.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Metal Blocks - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Use Metal Blocks for durable frames and protected machinery while controlling vehicle weight in Scrap Mechanic. Check the related systems first.

name: Concrete Blocks
description: Heavy construction blocks suited to stationary defenses, foundations, and structures that benefit from mass.
imageAlt: concrete blocks image from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Mass Is Useful When It Has a Job
paragraphs: Concrete can stabilize a fixed structure and make barriers harder to push around. The same weight can make a mobile creation slow, unstable, and costly to recover.
bullets: Anchor defenses to a coherent foundation.
Leave paths for repair and crop access.
Use a lighter vehicle to service a heavy base.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Concrete Blocks - Uses and Guide
seo.description: In Scrap Mechanic, use Concrete Blocks for foundations, barriers, and stationary defense without overloading mobile builds. Verify the current role in-game.

name: Cardboard Block
description: A very light and fragile block useful for mockups, breakable targets, and mechanisms where low mass matters.
imageAlt: cardboard block image from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Build for Failure on Purpose
paragraphs: Cardboard is useful when a part should be easy to remove or destroy. It is a testing material, not reliable protection for a seat, engine, storage chest, or farm wall.
bullets: Use it to check size before spending stronger blocks.
Keep it away from the load path of a moving machine.
Replace the final prototype sections that must survive impact.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Cardboard Block - Uses and Guide
seo.description: Use Cardboard Blocks for lightweight mockups, breakable targets, and low-mass experiments in Scrap Mechanic. Check the related systems first.

name: Glass Block
description: A transparent building block crafted from Sand Blocks and Ember, used wherever a recipe needs a clear structural material.
imageAlt: Glass Block item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Turn Sand into a Workshop Material
paragraphs: Glass Block is the refining step between Sand Block collection and a large set of windows, lamps, containers, and machine recipes. Keep Ember beside the Craftbot so a missing single unit does not halt a full glass batch.

sections.heading: Plan the Batch Before Building
bullets: One Craftbot batch converts 10 Sand Blocks and 1 Ember into 10 Glass Blocks.
Reserve recipe stock before using the same Glass Blocks as decoration.
Use the recipe list below to check the exact variant and quantity a machine consumes.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Glass Block Recipe and Uses
seo.description: Check the Scrap Mechanic Glass Block recipe, Sand Block and Ember cost, current block properties, and every matching Craftbot use in Survival.

name: Plastic Block
description: A light, buoyant building material made from Crude Oil and consumed by many utility-part recipes.
imageAlt: Plastic Block item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Convert Oil in Useful Batches
paragraphs: Plastic Block turns collected Crude Oil into a general workshop material. Because a five-oil craft returns ten blocks, plan demand by output batch instead of treating every block as a separate oil cost.

sections.heading: Keep Structural and Recipe Stock Separate
bullets: Use its low weight and high buoyancy where those properties help the build.
Keep a labeled reserve for parts that explicitly require Plastic Block.
Check the live recipe panel before committing a decorative stockpile.

seo.title: Scrap Mechanic Plastic Block Recipe and Uses
seo.description: See the Scrap Mechanic Plastic Block recipe, Crude Oil batch cost, current physical properties, and parts that consume Plastic Blocks in Survival.

name: Sand Block
description: A dense raw building block refined from Scrap Stone Block and used as the main Craftbot input for Glass Block.
imageAlt: Sand Block item icon from Scrap Mechanic

sections.heading: Read Sand as a Refining Stage
paragraphs: Sand Block is both a placeable material and the upstream input for Glass Block. The Craftbot doubles the block count when it converts five Scrap Stone Blocks into ten Sand Blocks, but the following glass step still needs Ember.

sections.heading: Use the Right Supply Route
bullets: Craft it from Scrap Stone Block when refining collected material.
The Farmers Hideout trade data also lists a 500-block Sand reward for one Redbeet Crate.
Calculate Glass Block demand first so the Ember requirement is not missed.
